chapter: Tape two: Tom Brown and the Dixieland band
title: Johnny Frisco and Jules Cassard
summary: Lala and the visitors remember the drummer Johnny Frisco, called Mulefoot, and the multi-instrumentalist Jules Cassard.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: He used to play with Bromley. Do you remember we played on the boat? On the Capitol? When they had the Battle of Bands, when all the four bands were there.
Johnny would shoot him like a double ending, he'd take him on the car bells there. Oh, what a crumb. I can't remember what that means.
Frisco, huh? Johnny Frisco, yeah. Johnny Frisco. He used to call him Mulefoot. You know what he's doing now? Johnny Frisco? No.
He said Jules Cassard played trombone.

Jules Cassard played trombone, yeah. Right? That's the same one? Yeah. That's his cousin. His uncle. His uncle, yeah. Jules played trombone, yeah. He played trombone, yeah. He got songwriters in the family. I see you. Talk about a sweet barricone, that song could play a sweet barricone too. And you ought to see him on the piano too. Everything is well accompanied. And he played a violin, played a wonderful guitar. He played trombone. Did he go away with no Jews? No. The Jews went away a long time ago. I thought he stayed around the lawn. Yeah. I thought he stayed around the lawn. Yeah.
